answer.rationale: Current onboarding completion is down 4% QoQ and activation is down 6% QoQ. Memory_86 and memory_31 both show direct evidence that simplifying/shortening onboarding drives measurable improvements in completion rates and early activation—precisely the metrics now declining. This is the highest-confidence lever available. Verifying these two memories will validate whether the original conditions and effect sizes hold at current scale. While promotional_pricing could address competitor pressure, memory_73 shows dangerous retention risk (-12%) that conflicts with the primary objective of sustainable revenue. Enterprise_sales_assist is strong (memory_44) but doesn't address the systemic activation decline. Referral_incentive (memory_57) works well for established customers but doesn't solve the current early-funnel problem. Activation_messaging (memory_91) showed gains but is smaller in magnitude than onboarding improvements. The strategic play is to reverse the activation/completion declines with the highest-confidence intervention, then defend against price competition through superior product experience rather than discounting. One standard experiment on onboarding simplification this week.
